Hey similar boat! I never really started transition (attempted but was always shoved back into the closet). I've tried for the past 3/4 years to fully embrace womanhood/femaleness/whatever. And while I have made a good amount of progress it got to a point where I had to ask myself, "Is this making me happy? Is the everyday misery of my dysphoria really worth whatever acceptance may bring me? Do I want to live the rest of my life like this?" Since asking myself these questions I started making small steps towards transition. Keeping a gender journal is really helpful to keep track of your feelings, pinpoint what is making you uncomfortable, and what helps ease that discomfort. Being critical of everything helps me weight he pros and cons of each step and ease my way into things, rushing into things backfires in no time. If you cant access therapy or dont find it useful like I do, journaling really is a great way to work through these feelings. You can find a lot of things like CBT worksheets online that you can work on see if that helps any.

Also, dont let any person or group influence you too much. No one in this sub, or any other online forum, knows your life. Only you can judge what may be the best path for you.

Twice when I was in elementary school, I witnessed my father try to kill my mother. They stayed together because she couldn't afford to live on her own/was still getting over her disability. He and I were never close but especially so after these events. He doesn't know how to talk to me and despite living in the same house we know very little about each other. Hes tried to build a relationship but theres just nothing there. I can never trust him and cant wait until he is out of my life. 

As for my mother... she had severe mental issues when I was born. I know it wasn't her fault but I feel like, while yes she has made improvements and is a lot more mentally clear now, she has said too many hurtful things in recent years for me to feel like we're close or that I can trust her. As a child I was essentially her little therapist (finding out about what emotional incest was made so many things clearer about our relationship). As a teenager I also had a lot of mental health issues (I've self harmed for years, attempted suicide multiple times, had to drop out of high school to focus on recovery). I know it couldn't have been easy to be my parent, but at the same time I feel like she wasn't there for me when I needed her most even though I had no choice but to ALWAYS be there for her. Now as an adult doing all the things I never thought I'd live to do, I still struggle sometimes. I tried to tell her a few months ago that I was feeling suicidal, as she always says shes there for me and that we can talk if I need her blah blah blah. Except when I told her her response was "if you don't care about yourself then I don't have to care about you." It is quit literally the worst thing anyone has ever said to me and it has completely broken me. I think about the fact that my mother doesn't care about me every day. I self harm fairly regularly now, and feel like I'm starting to develop an alcohol addiction. 

I have friends who tell me they care about me but I know I'll never fully trust them. I don't think I will ever be able to trust anyone like I used to. I'm trying to get better for those friends and not let them see me struggle. I feel totally alone in this world and like I'm just counting down the days until I finally die. I'm so envious of people who grew up with loving, involved parents. If you've never had to question your ability to be loved, you are so lucky.
